topic: Commissioning timeline and sponsor restructuring (status as of mid-2026)
wiki_text: As of mid-2026 the Puerto Sandino FSRU import terminal remains under construction. New Fortress Energy's early-2026 investor update listed Nicaragua terminal commissioning among its 2026 outlook, targeting October 2026 - roughly five years after the project's original 2021 in-service goal and following repeated slips (2H2021, then Q4 2024, then Q1 2025). The associated ~300 MW Puerto Sandino power plant has been reported as essentially complete (100%); remaining work centers on the maritime/jetty and pipeline scope and final FSRU deployment. NFE has a long-term LNG supply arrangement for the project sourced mainly from U.S. liquefaction (an LNG supply agreement reported to run through 2027), with project operations variously described as commencing across 2027-2029. Concurrently, NFE is undertaking a major creditor-led debt restructuring (~US$5.7bn) under a UK restructuring plan and intends to split into a privately held 'BrazilCo' (creditor-owned Brazil assets) and a publicly traded 'New NFE' that would retain its Nicaragua, Puerto Rico and Mexico assets, including Puerto Sandino.
reverify_note: Re-sourced off-GEM. October 2026 target + 'New NFE' split + ~US$5.7bn UK restructuring (Nicaragua/PR/Mexico retained) corroborated by quartr (NFE investor update) and offshore-mag (independent). 100% power-plant completion + timeline slips + vessels corroborated by lngprime and gasoutlook. LNG supply through 2027 corroborated by seekingalpha. CORRECTED the prior draft's '20-year terms commencing 2027 and 2029' claim: not corroborable off-GEM as worded; sources describe an LNG supply agreement running through 2027 and project operations described across 2027-2029, so the wiki_text was rephrased to match the sourced language.

wiki_text: Reporting on the Puerto Sandino regasification vessel is not fully consistent. In November 2024 NFE CEO Wes Edens described the 125,856-cbm 'Energos Freeze' as the FSRU bound for Puerto Sandino (then completing work at the Navantia yard in El Ferrol, Spain, and due to deploy on exiting dry dock at end-2024). Other coverage references the 138,000-cbm 'Energos Princess' serving as the floating storage unit (FSU) at the jetty, implying a possible two-vessel FSU+FSRU arrangement. The Energos Freeze assignment is now in doubt: in May 2025 NFE executed a three-year charter for the Energos Freeze for the Dominican Republic (Pepillo Salcedo/Manzanillo, Energia 2000), not Nicaragua. GEM currently records the floating vessel as 'Energos Princess'. The deployed regas vessel name and IMO should be confirmed from NFE IR / vessel tracking before the GEM vessel field is changed.
verification_status: [CONFLICTING DATA — Energos Freeze identity 2-corroborated; Energos Princess FSU single-publisher (yellow)]
reverify_note: Re-sourced off-GEM. The 125,856-cbm 'Energos Freeze' FSRU identity is corroborated by two independent publishers (lngprime + lngindustry); lngindustry further confirms the May 2025 Energos Freeze 3-year charter was for the Dominican Republic (Pepillo Salcedo/Manzanillo), strengthening the doubt that it is the Nicaragua vessel. The GEM-recorded '138,000-cbm Energos Princess' FSU detail only verifies (url_verifier, token 'Energos Princess'+'138,000') on LNG Prime reporting — a single publisher — so this point is downgraded to yellow/single-source; gasoutlook discusses the project but does not surface the vessel names/capacities to the verifier (dynamic content) and was dropped. Recommendation unchanged: confirm deployed regas vessel name + IMO from NFE IR / vessel tracking before editing the GEM vessel field.
